configurePresets.name: debug
configurePresets.description: Unoptimised build with assertions. The default for working on the code.

configurePresets.name: release
configurePresets.description: Optimised build with debug information. Every performance figure the project quotes comes from this configuration, and the debug information is kept because a profile of a binary without it names addresses rather than functions.

configurePresets.name: sanitise
configurePresets.description: Instrumented build for the sanitiser run in the definition of done. Optimisation is kept on because an unoptimised sanitiser build is slow enough that the suite stops being run, and the frame pointers needed for readable reports are restored explicitly.

configurePresets.name: thread-sanitise
configurePresets.description: Instrumented build for the data race check the scheduler in Phase 6 makes necessary. It is a separate preset because the thread sanitiser cannot be combined with the address sanitiser, and optimisation is kept on for the same reason the other sanitiser preset keeps it: an instrumented suite slow enough to be skipped is a check that is not performed.

configurePresets.name: single-precision
configurePresets.description: Release with float rather than double as the scalar type. It exists as a preset rather than a manual flag because the throughput-oriented configuration has to be built and tested as often as the accuracy-oriented one.

configurePresets.name: sycl
configurePresets.description: Release with the GPU backend built. Requires the oneAPI DPC++ compiler, which is not one of the three the project is otherwise tested with, so the compiler has to be selected explicitly: set CXX or pass -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER. On Windows that is icx-cl, the MSVC-style driver, because CMake drives a Windows IntelLLVM compiler with MSVC-style flags and icpx rejects them. Elsewhere it is icpx. Run the oneAPI environment script first so the compiler is on PATH.

configurePresets.name: sycl-single-precision
configurePresets.displayName: Release with the SYCL backend, single precision
configurePresets.description: The configuration the GPU figures in docs/performance/sycl_direct.md are taken in. It exists as a preset of its own because the throughput-oriented configuration is the one a large GPU run uses, and the accuracy it costs is measured against the double-precision CPU reference rather than assumed.

configurePresets.name: cuda
configurePresets.description: Release with the second GPU backend built. Requires the CUDA toolkit, so that nvcc is on PATH or CUDACXX names it, and nothing else: the host compiler stays whichever one the build would otherwise use, because only the two kernel translation units go through the device compiler. The kernels are compiled for the architectures in ORRERY_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES, which defaults to Turing, so a build for a different card passes its own. No device is needed to build or to run the suite: the CUDA cases skip themselves where there is nothing to run them on.

configurePresets.name: cuda-single-precision
configurePresets.displayName: Release with the CUDA backend, single precision
configurePresets.description: The configuration the figures in docs/performance/cuda.md are taken in. It exists as a preset of its own for the reason the SYCL one does: the throughput-oriented configuration is the one a large GPU run uses, and on a consumer NVIDIA card the gap between the two precisions is a hardware ratio rather than a rounding question, so the two have to be measured separately rather than assumed to differ by a constant.

configurePresets.name: renderer
configurePresets.description: Release with the viewer and the offline frame export built. It fetches GLFW and needs an OpenGL 3.3 driver, so it is a preset of its own rather than part of the default build: a machine with no display can still build and test everything else, including the parts of the visualisation layer that are arithmetic. This is the configuration docs/visualisation.md quotes.

configurePresets.name: python
configurePresets.description: Release with the extension module built into build/python/python/orrery, which is a directory that can be put on PYTHONPATH and imported without installing anything. Needs a Python interpreter with its development headers, and NumPy and pytest for the suite. Building a wheel does not use this preset: pip drives CMake itself through scikit-build-core.

configurePresets.name: wasm
configurePresets.description: The browser module: core, initial conditions, integrators and the CPU solvers, compiled to WebAssembly through the Emscripten toolchain and reached through the C interface in wasm/. Needs emsdk on the environment, so run its emsdk_env script first, which sets EMSDK. The renderer, the SYCL backend, the command-line programs and the library's file I/O are not part of this build; the tests and benchmarks are not either, since a browser is not where they are run. Writes the module into web/public/solver.

configurePresets.name: lint
configurePresets.description: Runs clang-tidy alongside the compiler, so lint sees exactly the flags the code is compiled with rather than a reconstruction of them. Requires Clang as the compiler.
